title: The quick open dialog interaction feel should be harmonized (mouse pointer, button styles among others)
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.6-dev3 ### System information Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS ### Issue description The quick open script dialog's interaction feels a little off in comparison to the rest of Godot and desktop applications in general. Every interactive element shows a pointer cursor, which is more a web thing; less a desktop application standard. IMHO the pointer cursor should be sparingly used, only for hypertext links or things that have a really low affordance. Interactive elements should use the normal arrow cursor instead, like the rest of Godot buttons and toolbars. The button to toggle between the list and grid mode does not have the hover highlight rectangle like other toolbar buttons. In addition, by having a look at the source code, the measurements of this dialog seem not to take into account the spacing settings (compact vs spacious or custom values) set by the user or the theme. Everything is hardcoded. ### Steps to reproduce Create a blank project. Create a couple empty gdscript files. Create a new 2d scene. From the inspector, at the very bottom, click the folder button next to the script entry. The dialog opens and you can interact with it, seeing the things I mentioned. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) N/A
